test_title: PYST 10: Selection Post (Matric Level) - GA (Held On 01 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What does HDI stand for?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Human Development Index**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **HDI** stands for **Human Development Index**, which is a statistical composite index used to measure the average achievements of a country in three basic dimensions of human development. ***Hence, the correct answer is Human Development Index.***

• The concept of the **Human Development Index** was created by the Pakistani economist **Mahbub ul Haq** and the Indian economist **Amartya Sen** in **1990**.

• It is published annually by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** as part of the **Human Development Report (HDR)**.

• The index was designed to shift the focus of development economics from national income accounting to people-centered policies, emphasizing that people and their capabilities should be the ultimate criteria for assessing the development of a country.

• It ranks countries into four levels of human development: **Very High**, **High**, **Medium**, and **Low** based on their cumulative score across various indicators.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Health Dimension**: This is assessed by **Life Expectancy at birth**, which is the average number of years a person is expected to live based on current mortality rates. It serves as a proxy for the overall health and nutrition status of a population.

• **Education Dimension**: This is calculated using two indicators: **Mean years of schooling** (the average number of years of education received by people ages **25** and older) and **Expected years of schooling** (the total number of years of schooling that a child of school-entry age can expect to receive).

• **Standard of Living**: This is assessed by **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita** at **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)** in international **US Dollars**. This measure accounts for the differences in the cost of living and inflation between countries.

• The **HDI** score is a value between **0 and 1**. A score closer to **1** indicates a higher level of development, while a score closer to **0** indicates a lower level.

• The **UNDP** uses the **geometric mean** of the three normalized dimension indices to calculate the final **HDI** value, ensuring that a low achievement in one dimension is not linearly compensated by a high achievement in another.

**Important Points__**

• In the latest **Human Development Report 2023-24**, **India** was ranked **134th** out of **193 countries** with an **HDI** value of **0.644**, placing it in the **Medium** human development category.

• **Switzerland**, **Norway**, and **Iceland** consistently rank at the top of the global **Human Development Index** due to their high life expectancy and robust social security systems.

• The **UNDP** also tracks other vital indices like the **Gender Inequality Index (GII)**, where **India** ranked **108th** in the **2022** report, showing improvement in gender parity.

• The **Inequality-adjusted Human Development Index (IHDI)** accounts for the distribution of achievements within a population; the difference between the **HDI** and **IHDI** represents the loss in human development due to inequality.

• The **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)** complements the **HDI** by identifying overlapping deprivations at the household and individual level in health, education, and living standards, providing a more comprehensive view of poverty than income alone.
